Problem Statement

A company has N organizations numbered 0 through N−1, with organization 0 at the top. Every organization i other than 0 has parent p_i. Repeatedly following parents always reaches 0. Each organization waits until it has received every report from its direct children, adds one report of its own, and sends all reports to its parent. A leaf sends its own single report immediately. Organization 0 submits its reports to the president. Find how many reports each organization submits. Complete the recursive function num_report(children,x); children[x] lists the direct children of organization x.

Constraints

1≤N≤50; 0≤p_i≤N−1 for 1≤i≤N−1; following parents from any organization reaches 0; all input values are integers.

Input

N
p_1 p_2 p_3 \ldots p_{N - 1}

Output

Print N lines. On line i+1, for 0≤i<N, print the number of reports submitted by organization i. For organization 0, count the reports submitted to the president.

Starter Program

# Return the number of reports submitted by organization x
def num_report(children, x):
    # Complete the recursive function here

# The following lines need no changes
N = int(input())
# p[i]: the parent of organization i
# Organization 0 has no parent; use -1
# The input omits organization 0; prepend [-1] using list concatenation
p = [-1] + [int(c) for c in input().split()] 

# children[i] lists the direct children of organization i
children = [[] for _ in range(N)]
for i in range(1, N):
    parent = p[i] # parent is the parent of organization i
    children[parent].append(i) # Add i to the list of children of parent

# Compute and print the answer for each organization
for i in range(N):
    res = num_report(children, i)
    print(res)

Problem Statement

Given integers A and B with 0≤A,B≤255, find a nonnegative integer C such that A xor C=B. It can be proved that C exists uniquely and satisfies 0≤C≤255. Bitwise xor sets a binary digit to 1 exactly when that digit is 1 in one of the two operands and 0 in the other; otherwise it sets it to 0. For example, 3 xor 5=6 because 011 xor 101=110 in binary. This exercise is adapted from ABC213A and uses different tests.

Constraints

0≤A,B≤255; all input values are integers.

Input

A B

Output

Print C.

Sample Input 1

3 6

Sample Output 1

5

3 is 011 in binary and 5 is 101. Their xor is 110, which is 6 in decimal, so the answer is 5.

Sample Output 2

6
